articles.title: Melioidosis, a Deadly Soil Infection That Mimics TB, Is Going Undetected Across India
articles.excerpt: A 15-centre Lancet study found the infection in 8.9% of high-risk hospital patients, and one in five died. The disease is not notifiable in India, labs routinely misidentify the bacterium, and standard TB treatment does not work against it.
articles.image_caption: Colonies of Burkholderia pseudomallei, the soil bacterium that causes melioidosis, growing on Ashdown agar. The infection mimics tuberculosis and is going undetected across India.

articles.excerpt: Police registered FIR No. 259/2026 at Police Station Handwara, said the investigation has revealed suspected involvement of overground workers and others, and said efforts are underway to identify and arrest the remaining persons involved.
articles.nri_angle: This is a local law-and-order development in north Kashmir with no direct diaspora dimension; it is relevant to diaspora readers with roots in Jammu and Kashmir following security developments there.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Cancels Probation for Convicts in Brutal 2003 Bahraich Attack
articles.excerpt: Justices Pardiwala and Chandran held that the High Court granted probation under the Probation of Offenders Act despite an adverse probation report and without weighing the nature of the offence, and ordered both men to surrender within two weeks.
articles.nri_angle: This is a domestic Indian criminal-justice ruling with no direct diaspora dimension; it is relevant to diaspora readers following how Indian courts treat probation in violent offences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Flags Three-Month Delay in TMC Rebel MPs' Disqualification Case
articles.excerpt: A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant called the lapse of three months a red flag, kept Abhishek Banerjee's petition alive to monitor the Speaker's proceedings, and recorded that the 20 MPs would file replies within four weeks.
articles.nri_angle: This is a domestic Indian parliamentary dispute with no direct diaspora dimension; it matters to diaspora readers following anti-defection law and West Bengal politics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Poland Set 2030 Trade Goal, Deepen Defence and Space Ties
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk agreed in New Delhi on Thursday to double bilateral trade by 2030, press for early implementation of the India-EU free trade agreement, and expand co-development in defence, space and energy.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi holds a bilateral meeting with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House, New Delhi, on October 22, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For Indians in Europe and North America, a stronger India-Poland partnership and an India-EU trade deal shape the business and job links many diaspora firms use to enter Central and Eastern Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Leaders meet and agree on trade goals

articles.title: India Rejects UN Report Calling Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company 'India-Based'
articles.excerpt: New Delhi told a UN committee the description ignores the Security Council's own record: Dawood Ibrahim has been wanted in India for terror attacks since 1993 and fled the country long before his 2003 listing.
articles.image_caption: An Indian diplomat addresses the UN General Assembly Third Committee from the India seat in New York. India rejected a UN rapporteur report describing Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company as an India-based group.
articles.nri_angle: India is pressing the UN to correct how it describes a fugitive wanted for the 1993 Mumbai attacks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mysuru Dasara Ends With 417th Jamboo Savari Led by Elephant Prashanth
articles.excerpt: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar flagged off the Vijayadashami finale at Mysore Palace, as Prashanth carried the 750-kg golden howdah to Bannimantap for the first time as lead elephant.
articles.nri_angle: The Jamboo Savari finale is the defining Dasara spectacle for the Kannada diaspora, preserving the Wadiyar-era royal procession as Karnataka's state festival.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Houses Torched in Deserted Kuki Village in Manipur's Kamjong District
articles.excerpt: Suspected militants set fire to homes in Khoikai village near Chassad early on Wednesday; no casualties were reported as residents had already fled amid worsening Kuki-Naga clashes.
articles.nri_angle: Fresh arson in Kamjong extends Manipur's Kuki-Naga violence and displacement that diaspora families from the state continue to follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

15 houses burned in Chassad village

articles.title: Delhi-NCR Imposes GRAP-1 Curbs as Air Quality Slips to Poor
articles.excerpt: CAQM invoked GRAP Stage-I across Delhi-NCR on October 21 after Delhi's AQI rose from 179 to 244, with poor air forecast to continue in coming days.
articles.image_caption: Smog over Delhi. The capital's AQI rose to 244 on October 21, prompting GRAP Stage-I curbs across Delhi-NCR.
articles.nri_angle: Delhi-NCR air curbs affect diaspora families with relatives in the capital as the winter pollution season begins.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Seeks FSSAI Reply on Analogue Products Sold as Paneer
articles.excerpt: A bench gave the Centre, FSSAI and Delhi government six weeks to respond to a PIL targeting non-dairy substitutes passed off as paneer without disclosure, while declining interim enforcement directions.
articles.nri_angle: Paneer is a staple for diaspora households and festival cooking; the disclosure fight in Delhi shapes labelling norms Indian families rely on when buying or ordering paneer dishes in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: FSSAI draft amendment published
Action at Okhla Sabzi Mandi destroying 508 kg of suspected spurious paneer

articles.title: Supreme Court Stays CMRL Probe Against Pinarayi Vijayan for One Week
articles.excerpt: A vacation bench paused the investigation — not the FIR — so the former Kerala chief minister, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law P A Mohamed Riyas can appeal to the High Court division bench.
articles.nri_angle: The case against a former Kerala chief minister and his family is closely followed by the large Keralite diaspora in the US and Gulf for what it signals about governance in the state.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dr Reddy's Wins DCGI Approval for Zytorvi in Advanced Esophageal Cancer
articles.excerpt: The CDSCO approval makes Zytorvi, with cisplatin and paclitaxel, a first-line option for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in India — its second indication in the country.
articles.image_caption: Dr Reddy's development center in Hyderabad. The company won DCGI approval for Zytorvi in advanced esophageal cancer.
articles.nri_angle: The approval expands first-line immunotherapy access in India for a cancer that was the country's fourth leading cause of cancer death in 2024.

articles.title: AAP Claims Bhagwant Mann Held Three Hours at Delhi Airport, Fined Rs 50,000
articles.excerpt: The party alleges the Punjab chief minister was delayed on return from a court-cleared Paris trade trip and fined by officials citing 'pressure from above'; authorities have not responded.
articles.image_caption: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann speaks from his office. AAP alleged Mann was held for three hours at Delhi airport on his return from Paris and fined Rs 50,000.
articles.nri_angle: For Punjab's large diaspora, the episode extends a documented Centre-state fight over the chief minister's foreign travel — a clearance denial overturned by the High Court preceded this airport claim.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.event: Mann attended SIAL Paris food exhibition
AAP alleged Mann was detained at Delhi Airport

articles.title: Indian-Origin Couple Sentenced in UK Over Fake Covid PPE Deals
articles.excerpt: Jogesh Bhandari was jailed for eight years and his wife given a suspended sentence after a five-week trial over nitrile-glove contracts that were paid for and never delivered.
articles.nri_angle: A UK diaspora fraud prosecution closes with an eight-year sentence — a reminder that pandemic-era emergency contracts are still being audited and prosecuted years later.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Florida Store Owner Charged With Murder After Teen E-Bike Rider Dies
articles.excerpt: West Melbourne police say Kavan Patel, 32, intentionally struck 14-year-old Hunter Russey after a store burglary alarm and left him in a ditch; the boy died days later.
articles.image_caption: Police booking photo of Kavan Patel and a photo of Hunter Russey are shown over the Corner Store in West Melbourne, Florida. Patel faces a second-degree murder charge after Russey died from injuries sustained on October 13.
articles.nri_angle: A diaspora convenience-store owner faces a homicide prosecution after police say he pursued a suspected burglar himself instead of calling law enforcement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Patel re-arrested and charged with second-degree murder.

articles.title: Two British Indian Men Assaulted Outside Dussehra, Bathukamma Celebration in West Yorkshire
articles.excerpt: The attack outside Ossett Town Hall on October 17 left both men bleeding, police are treating the assaults as racially aggravated, and organisers are pressing for CCTV to be secured before it is overwritten.
articles.image_caption: Ossett Town Hall in West Yorkshire. Two British Indian men were assaulted outside the hall during a Dussehra and Bathukamma celebration.
articles.nri_angle: A racially aggravated attack at a family festival in West Yorkshire is a direct safety concern for British Indian communities planning the rest of the festival season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi at Delhi Dussehra: Unite, Defeat Enemies, Govern as Ram Rajya
articles.excerpt: At the Ravana Dahan in IP Extension on October 20, Prime Minister Narendra Modi defined India's enemies as forces that harm its honour, divide society and hate its culture, and held up Ram Rajya — no discrimination, equal justice and power as service — as the standard for governance and self-reliant development.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian Americans staging Ramlilas and Ravana Dahan at temples and community grounds for Vijayadashami, Modi's Delhi speech links the festival they celebrate abroad directly to debates at home over unity, cultural heritage and what good governance owes the poorest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Seeks All-Party Meeting After Manipur Civilian Killings
articles.excerpt: A delegation led by former Chief Minister Okram Ibobi Singh urged Chief Minister Khemchand Singh to convene all parties after three firewood collectors were killed in Imphal East; the Chief Minister assured them the demand would be looked into.
articles.nri_angle: Renewed violence and shutdowns in Manipur directly affect Manipuri families in the US and elsewhere who travel home and follow the state's security situation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Warns Gulf Situation Is Deep Concern in UAE Talks
articles.excerpt: Meeting UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Mumbai, Jaishankar backed dialogue, unimpeded energy and trade flows, and noted bilateral trade has crossed $100 billion since the CEPA.
articles.nri_angle: Jaishankar thanked the UAE leadership for ensuring the well-being of the large Indian community in the UAE, making diaspora welfare a formal item in the Mumbai talks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Early Flu Season and Mutated H1N1 Strain Raise Concern for Younger Americans
articles.excerpt: CDC data show flu positivity at 5.0% nationally and 10.7% on the West Coast, with H1N1 accounting for 96.4% of subtyped flu A viruses. Doctors recommend vaccination for everyone 6 months and older before the end of October.
articles.image_caption: An electron micrograph of the influenza virus. Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 is the dominant strain in CDC data this season.
articles.nri_angle: Multigenerational Indian American households with young children and older parents face the combined risk the data highlight, making October vaccination for every eligible family member the practical step.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Celebrating Dussehra / Vijayadashami: A Festival of Victory and Goodness
articles.excerpt: Dussehra marks the triumph of good over evil in Indian culture.
articles.image_caption: Dussehra festival celebrations at Jakhu Temple. Dussehra (Vijayadashami) marks the victory of Rama over Ravana.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Rappers Turn Water Shortages and Heat Into a Climate Alarm
articles.excerpt: Kali, Abisha of Sollisai Sistahs and four other young artistes have released the six-track Climate Emergency Mixtape, billed as India's first multilingual rap album about the climate crisis.
articles.image_caption: A performer raps on stage in front of a Climate Emergency Mixtape backdrop during the album launch. The six-track album is billed by its organisers as India's first multilingual rap album about the climate crisis.
articles.nri_angle: A multilingual Indian rap album about water, heat and floods gives diaspora listeners the climate crisis in the languages and neighbourhoods of home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rajnath Singh Represents India at SCO Heads of Government Meeting in Dushanbe
articles.excerpt: India's defence minister met Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref in Dushanbe, and used his SCO address to call for an end to double standards on terrorism.
articles.image_caption: India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh shakes hands with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda in front of an SCO backdrop in Dushanbe. Singh represented India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting on October 19-20, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India's defence minister leading New Delhi's delegation at the SCO in Dushanbe signals how India is engaging Central Asia on trade, connectivity and security.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Orders Mandatory Insurance on All Railway Counter Tickets From October 27
articles.excerpt: In an October 6 order arising from the 2023 Odisha train accident, the Supreme Court directed Indian Railways to extend its 45-paise travel insurance scheme to tickets bought at station counters — mandatory from October 27, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of diaspora families travel by train in India, especially around Diwali; counter-bought tickets now carry the same accident cover as online bookings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: British Tourist Harassed in Varkala, Dress Torn; Her Own Video Leads Police to Arrest
articles.excerpt: Police identified the accused, Shahad of Odayam, from a video the woman recorded during the 1:30 a.m. attack; he was set to be produced in court Tuesday for remand.
articles.image_caption: Varkala, Kerala, where a British tourist was allegedly harassed while walking back to her room late on Monday.
articles.nri_angle: Kerala is a top destination for diaspora families and international visitors alike; a street attack on a tourist in Varkala puts visitor safety in the state under scrutiny.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Court Extends Detention of 'Cockroach' Leaders Ranka and Das by Two Days
articles.excerpt: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, arrested after entering the newly banned Jantar Mantar protest site, will stay in custody while police question them further. Their party is demanding the election chief's resignation over the voter-list revision.
articles.nri_angle: The protests over India's voter-list revision, and the detention of the youth leaders driving them, are the central domestic political story diaspora readers are following from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
